$comment: The Optical Leveller's parameters, declared once.
Both the C++ dispatch and the TypeScript control table are generated from
What is *not* here is as important as what is. There is no threshold, no
knee and no ratio, because the unit has none: section 5 says the local ratio
is a continuous function of level and of how long that level has been
present, and that an implementation computing `if (level > threshold)` has
already diverged from the reference. PEAK REDUCTION sets how hard the
sidechain drives the panel and the loop does the rest.

params.name: Peak Reduction
params.note: The panel's 0-100 scale, normalised. Section 3.1 says the numbers correspond to no dB value and the taper is unknown, so this is dimensionless and its mapping to reduction is whatever the loop makes it.

params.name: Gain
params.note: Outside the detector loop, which section 3.2 marks as inference and test 12 checks: sweeping this must move the reduction by under a decibel.

params.name: Mode
params.note: A change in the sidechain's gain and rectification law, never a ratio parameter. Section 3.3: a ratio computed from a static curve is right at one depth and wrong at all others.

params.name: Emphasis
params.note: Internal on the hardware and factory-set flat. Exposed here as most modern equivalents do, and defaulted flat so the baseline matches the unit as shipped.

params.name: Cell Wear
params.note: An explicit parameter rather than something baked in, as section 7 asks. All three published symptoms of a worn cell move together because they are one process.

params.name: Oversampling
Noise
params.note: Scales the manual's own figure: at 1 the floor is 75 dB below +10 dBm, which is 17 dB noisier than the Program EQ and is one of this unit's published characteristics. Its render-delta gate is -95 dBFS rather than the suite's -70 for the same reason the Program EQ's is -110 - the parameter's job is to sit below that.
